Trap rules

%
Opaque inks (metallics, opaque spots) always receive traps from every other colour regardless of luminance and never spread themselves.
Black & overprint
%
Overprinting black is written into the output PDF (op/OP, OPM 1) — no knockout under black, so misregistration can't open a gap.
Analysis & output
px
Original vector content is never rasterised. Traps are added as vector overprint objects in the exact plate inks (process or original spot colour space). Raster input keeps full native resolution, embedded losslessly.
Methods reference
Spread — the lighter object grows outward into the darker background (light text on dark).
Choke — the lighter background grows into the darker object, i.e. the dark object's knockout shrinks (dark text on light).
Overprint — ink prints on top without knocking out (default for 100% K).
Knockout — underlying inks removed where colours meet; these edges are what get trapped.
Spread and choke are chosen automatically per edge: the lighter (lower neutral density) side's unique inks are placed as an overprinting strip on the darker side. No trap is made where the colours already share enough common ink.
